title: Cheeky Knight
reviewNotes: Three branches, 25 exact positions from complete six-piece board; practice objective draw. Kc7, Nc6+, Ne5 and Nc4 reroute to Nxb6+/Nc8+ despite ...d1=Q. Independently extended forced repetitions produce claimable threefold repetition. Kd5 and an independent Nd4 reroute lose; source and independent comparisons distinguished.
transcript: The most hopeless of positions is also the best one to look for a great upset. In this situation, it is pretty clear that black is the only one standing to win this game with a pawn only three steps away from promoting and the king simply too far to stop it. And unfortunately, knights are famously very bad at stopping past pawns. This knight has no way to reach the pawn before it gets a queen. Or at least, that's what it seems like. But white does have an incredible way to save this position. And it all starts with the brilliant idea. King to C7. Now, this might seem to make no sense because after the pawn pushes and the knight gives a check, the king can simply go to the corner and now there are no more checks with this knight and the king cannot do anything. But this is only the beginning of a brilliant plan to reroute this knight to a better square. And that is why white plays the only move that saves this position. Knight to E5. Now, of course, attacking the pawn, which means that if the pawn wants to try and promote, it has to push. And white continues with knight to C4, again attacking the pawn. But now, of course, the pawn can just promote and get a new queen anyway. What's the difference? Well, here is the difference. We have rerouted the knight to a better square from which it can now give another check to the king and this king is boxed in. It only has one square that it can go to. But after that, we can give another check on C8. This queen can be as strong as it wants, but here, it's powerless. It has no influence on this corner of the board. And so, the knight is just going to force the king to repeat moves and eventually draw the game. If you love incredible chess, follow for more.
